text.t: Mitochondria make ATP, the cell's main energy-carrying molecule, from the chemical energy in glucose and other nutrients.

text.t: ATP synthase, a protein machine in the inner membrane. Its round head is about 9 nanometres across, and turning parts of it add a phosphate to ADP to make ATP.

text.t: Skeletal muscle cells are long and cylinder-shaped, so they are also called muscle fibres.

src.t: Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 10.2 Skeletal Muscle

text.t: Myofibrils are strands that run the whole length of the cell, built from repeating units called sarcomeres.

src.t: Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 10.2 Skeletal Muscle

text.t: Their actin and myosin filaments, lined up in order, give the cell its striped look.

src.t: Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 10.2 Skeletal Muscle

text.t: One repeat of the stripe pattern is called a sarcomere, and it holds two kinds of overlapping filament, thick and thin, that slide past each other when the muscle shortens.

text.t: Actin is one of the two proteins that make muscle contract, working together with myosin.

src.t: OpenStax Biology 2e, section 3.4 Proteins

text.t: Myosin is the other protein that drives muscle contraction, working together with actin.

src.t: OpenStax Biology 2e, section 3.4 Proteins

text.t: Red blood cells pick up oxygen in the lungs and carry it to the body's tissues, held by hemoglobin.

src.t: Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 18.3 Erythrocytes

text.t: Each hemoglobin molecule can carry four oxygen molecules, and one red blood cell may hold about 300 million of them.

src.t: Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 18.3 Erythrocytes

text.t: Hemoglobin is the protein that carries oxygen in the blood, packed inside red blood cells.

src.t: OpenStax Biology 2e, section 40.2 Components of the Blood

text.t: It is made of four protein chains, two alpha and two beta, and each chain holds a heme group with an iron atom.
